top_stories.title: Twisha Sharma death case: husband Samarth Singh brought to Bhopal, police to seek remand - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Samarth Singh**, the husband of Twisha Sharma, who was found dead in her marital home on May 12th, 2026, was arrested by **Madhya Pradesh police** after he surrendered at a Jabalpur district court.  He is being held for questioning regarding his alleged involvement in dowry death and harassment. The case has prompted the State government to recommend a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Sharma's death.  The investigation is ongoing, with **Giribala Singh**, former judge and chairperson of the Bhopal Consumer Court, stating she is willing to provide a statement but has not yet been contacted by police.

top_stories.title: TVK government will fall one day, says M.K. Stalin - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **M.K. Stalin**, leader of the **DMK**, criticized the **TVK** government, led by Chief Minister **C. Joseph Vijay**, for its dependence on other parties for support and alleged attempts to split the AIADMK.  He compared the public's interest in the new party to a child's fascination with a toy, predicting that it would fade quickly. **Stalin** also highlighted his government's achievements over the past five years as evidence of improved governance.

top_stories.title: DMK, Congress trade barbs over the latter’s post-poll alliance with the TVK - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **DMK** leader Udhayanidhi Stalin accused the **Congress** of being responsible for the BJP's victories, claiming they had "shed blood and tears" to ensure Congress wins.  **DMK** president M.K. Stalin was also present at the meeting where a resolution condemned the **Congress** for its betrayal and labeled it a "parasite".  The **Congress** Legislature Party leader S. Rajesh Kumar countered these accusations, stating that the people of Tamil Nadu elected the **AIADMK** to power based on the promise of sharing power with alliance partners.

top_stories.title: Coalition government here to stay in Tamil Nadu like Kerala, says Kader Mohideen - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **K.M. Kader Mohideen**, president of the **Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)**, stated that Tamil Nadu has formed a coalition government similar to Kerala and that it will continue in the future. He attributed this success to the DMK's ability to secure votes from the Muslim community, which he believes was crucial for their victory.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new leader of Tamil Nadu politics, is credited with initiating this change.

top_stories.title: Becoming a permanent resident in the US: List of top 10 countries that obtain maximum Green Cards - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **US Citizenship and Immigration Services** (USCIS) has announced a new rule requiring Green Card applicants to file their applications from consulates in their home countries, rather than within the US. This change, which experts say is not a law change but a minor tweak with significant impact, affects applicants who previously changed their status in the US while intending to become permanent residents. The new rule could significantly affect countries that receive the most Green Cards annually, including **Mexico**, **India**, **China**, and others, as it may delay processing times for those already facing long backlogs.

top_stories.title: Tens of thousands rally in Serbia for antigovernment demonstrations | Protests News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of people, led by student activists, rallied in Belgrade to protest against the Serbian government and demand early elections. The demonstrations, sparked by the November 2024 rail station disaster that killed 16 people, have grown into a campaign demanding President **Aleksandar Vucic** call for an election.  The protests were met with clashes between protesters and police, with some setting fire to bins filled with rubbish.  International organizations like the Council of Europe are monitoring the situation closely.

top_stories.title: Brampton man Gurkanwal Singh pleads guilty after shooting guns from jeep in 'careless and unsafe' stunt - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A 24-year-old Sikh man, **Gurkanwal Singh**, pleaded guilty to careless use of a firearm in Bracebridge court after videos showing him firing guns recklessly from a Jeep on Crown land in Ontario sparked an investigation. The incident occurred in February 2025 and involved the discovery of firearms inside the vehicle, with footage obtained from an Instagram account linked to **Singh**.  The case is expected to return to court later this month for sentencing.

top_stories.title: Iran move World Cup base from US to Mexico with FIFA approval | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Iran**'s football federation has moved their World Cup 2026 training camp from Arizona to Tijuana, Mexico, after receiving FIFA approval. **Mehdi Taj**, the federation president, stated that the move will help avoid visa complications stemming from the US-Israel war on Iran and allow for direct flights with **Iran Air**. The team will play their first two Group G matches in Los Angeles before facing Egypt in Seattle.

top_stories.title: Iran 'getting a lot closer' to agreement with US, Trump says
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** stated that **Iran** is "getting a lot closer" to reaching an agreement with the US on the war.  He has seen a draft agreement and insists any deal would prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, while Iranian foreign ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baqaei** said both sides have been converging in their positions but key issues remain unresolved. **Marco Rubio**, US Secretary of State, expressed cautious optimism about potential news within the next couple of days, emphasizing the US's stance on Iran not acquiring a nuclear weapon and reopening the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian tolls.  The temporary ceasefire between **Iran** and the US started in early April, with the US blockading Iranian ports since 13 April.

top_stories.title: China mine blast: Death toll rises to 82; Beijing orders crackdown as rescue ops continue — top developments - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A deadly gas explosion at a coal mine in Shanxi province, China has killed at least 82 people. The blast occurred on Friday evening at the Liushenyu mine, injuring over 120 others and leaving several missing.  **PM Modi** offered condolences to **President Xi Jinping** and the Chinese people. Authorities launched an investigation into the incident and vowed to crack down on illegal mining practices nationwide. Rescue operations are ongoing, with authorities deploying a large number of emergency personnel.
